name: Harvest 16-Bit
summary: Cozy SNES-era autumn farmland: warm hue-shifted pixel sprites, leaf-litter carpets, furrowed fields and wooden HUD panels.
description: A sunny autumn afternoon on the farm in true 16-bit pixel art: one art pixel per world unit, chunky 1-px coloured outlines, hue-shifted ramps that go plum in the shadows and butter-yellow in the light. Meadows in three greens, sunken dirt paths and furrowed soil fields, round orange/red/gold trees standing on carpets of fallen leaves. Every sprite is painted procedurally into a pixel grid with one shared top-left light, so the whole world reads like a hand-pixelled SNES farming RPG.

difficulty.why: Detailed 16-bit sprites with 4 walk frames as text grids are painstaking detail work, especially for large bosses.

technique.resolution: Low-res buffer at 1 art pixel = 1 world unit (360 units of height ≈ 360 or fewer buffer rows, integer upscale = round(screenH / 360)), nearest-neighbour upscale to the display.
technique.summary: Every sprite is computed into a small pixel grid at init: shapes are ellipses/tapered leaves whose sphere normals are lit by one fixed light (-0.5, -0.6, 0.62) and quantised into 3–5 step hue-shifted ramps, then an automatic 1-px outline is added using the darkened average colour of the neighbouring pixels. The ground is baked per 256-unit chunk as a material map (grass, golden grass, clover, soil, path) with pixel edge rules, stamped tufts and leaves, and decals.
technique.linework: 1-px outline on every sprite, never black: each empty pixel next to a filled one gets the average colour of its 4-neighbours mixed 58–84 % toward ink plum #24162a (brighter colours get darker outlines). Ghosts use a fixed cool outline #33406c, gems #6a2a1a, seeds #5e3a2a. No anti-aliasing, no sub-pixel lines, no canvas strokes.
technique.shading: Quantised Lambert: ramp index = how many thresholds the light value passes (typical thresholds [-0.22, 0.14, 0.5, 0.8]). Ramps are hue-shifted (pumpkin #74282a → #ffc76c, turnip purple #2c1740 → #bf80c8). Pumpkin ribs are 1-px curves one ramp step darker; tree canopies add value noise (±0.15) for leafy clumping; no smooth gradients inside sprites.
technique.lighting: One warm light from the top-left-front for every sprite. Glows are additive stepped discs (3 hard alpha rings) for gems, lanterns and carved faces. A full-screen soft-light grade (warm orange top-left → cool blue bottom-right, 50 %) plus a multiply plum vignette (#966e96 at the corners) sets the afternoon mood.
technique.texture: Pixel-level only: grass tufts (5 stamp shapes), clover trefoils, leaf-litter stamps, furrow stripes every 6 px in soil, per-pixel hashed light/dark specks on paths and soil, and a ±4.5 % macro warm/cool colour drift.

paletteRules: Every material is a 3–5 step hue-shifted ramp: shadows drift toward purple/plum, highlights toward yellow/cream. Never darken by mixing with black.
The ground is ~85 % greens (#77963b, #9a9d45, #5b893f) and warm browns; saturated orange/red/gold comes from trees and leaf carpets (~15–30 % of the screen).
Characters are warmer and more saturated than the ground: pumpkin orange, turnip purple, cream, ember yellow. Ghosts are the only cool colour on screen.
Glow colours (#f2902a, #ffc640, #fff2a8) appear only in carved faces, eyes, gems, lanterns and sparkles.
No pure black and no pure white except 1-px sparkle centres and the white hit-flash silhouette.
Outlines are always tinted versions of the object's own colour (mixed toward #24162a), never a uniform black line.

typography.css: font: 700 60px 'Pixelify Sans', monospace; color: #ffd36a; letter-spacing: 3px; text-shadow: 4px 0 #3b1d10, -4px 0 #3b1d10, 0 4px #3b1d10, 0 -4px #3b1d10, 4px 4px #3b1d10, -4px 4px #3b1d10, 4px -4px #3b1d10, -4px -4px #3b1d10, 0 8px #3b1d10;

typography.role: HUD numbers: HP text, kill counter, clock, level, key hints

background.summary: An endless autumn farmland baked per 256×256-unit chunk at 1 px per unit: noise-driven meadow patches in three greens, a winding sunken dirt path, rounded-rectangle ploughed fields with furrows and crop rows, and leaf-litter carpets under the trees, finished with pixel decals (flowers, mushrooms, pebbles, pumpkins, twigs).
layers: Material map per pixel: PATH (domain-warped Perlin iso-line, half width 8.5–14.5 units), SOIL (rounded-rectangle fields 150–290 × 96–190 units), else CLOVER / GOLD / GRASS from two fbm fields (scales 360 and 430 units) with a 64×64 tileable jitter so borders are ragged.
Pixel cleanup: remove 1-px spurs between height classes so edges are clean pixel art.

Detail stamps: grass tufts on a 7×6 grid (density driven by a 52-unit mottle noise), clover trefoils on a 5×4 grid, leaf stamps on a 3×3 grid whose survival depends on leaf density (organic carpet edges).

Colour pass with edge rules: bright rim on grass below a raised edge, dark lip above a drop, 2-px dithered shadow band where soil/path meet grass from above, furrow stripes (period 6) in soil, ruts and specks on paths.
Macro tint: multiply each pixel by 0.955–1.045 with a slight warm/cool shift from a 1100-unit noise.

Decals stamped deterministically across chunk borders: flowers (5 colours), tiny flowers, mushrooms near leaves, mini pumpkins and rocks in meadows, twigs, pebbles and edge stones on paths, sprout/turnip crop rows in fields. 's' pixels multiply the ground as a 1-px shadow.
Y-sorted props on top: autumn trees (56×65 / 68×80), hay bales, fences, scarecrows, stumps, wheelbarrows, crates.

characters.summary: Chibi 16-bit sprites about 22×30 px (hero) built in code: a big round head (about half the height) on a short body, ellipse forms lit by the shared light and quantised into hue-shifted ramps, details placed pixel by pixel, and an automatic coloured 1-px outline. Sprites face right; the left version is a mirrored copy. 4 walk frames (bob 0/-1, legs ±2 px, arm swing, cape/scarf flap) and 2 idle frames.
rules: Head-heavy chibi proportions: head ≈ 14 px tall on a 30 px sprite, legs 2 px wide, boots 3 px.
Every sprite gets the automatic coloured outline; never draw outlines by hand.
Faces glow: carved triangle eyes and jagged grins use the 3-step glow ramp with a 1-px dark cut lip above each hole.
Anchor every sprite at its feet (bottom centre) and draw it at integer coordinates.
Each enemy type owns one hue family: purple/magenta turnips, cold blue ghosts, ochre/purple brutes.
Paint every sprite facing right with the light from the top-left; the left-facing version is a plain mirrored copy (the light flips with it, which is invisible at this size).

effects.name: Seed projectile
effects.how: 5×3 cream seed sprite (4 rotation frames, outline #5e3a2a) plus two trailing 1-px dots #fff2c8 at 4 and 6 units behind with alpha 0.55 and 0.28.

effects.name: Hit flash + sparkle
effects.how: Enemy swaps to a pre-baked white silhouette while flash > 0.45; a 5×5 plus-shaped sparkle (#ffe9a0/#ffc84a/#ffffff) shrinks through 3 frames; leaves (2×2 particle frames) flutter off.

effects.name: Death burst
effects.how: 8 (brute: 16) square 2–3 px chunks in the enemy's ramp colours with a 1-px highlight, thrown up with gravity 200, plus 3–6 fluttering leaves, 2–5 dust puffs and an expanding 1-px pixel ring #fff4d0.

effects.name: Spawn from soil
effects.how: Enemies rise out of the ground: the sprite is cropped from the top (eased outQuad) above a 12×3 dirt mound sprite; dirt chunks #6e4632/#9a663f fly out. Ghosts instead fade in and sink 8 units with vapour puffs.

effects.name: XP gem
effects.how: 3×5 amber gem (big: 5×7 teal) bobbing 1 unit, over a tiny pixel shadow, with an additive stepped glow disc (r 3, #ff9030) pulsing 0.5±0.15 and a sparkle every ~1.25 s.

effects.name: Dash smear
effects.how: 3 afterimages tinted #ffc36a, spaced 7 units back along the dash, alpha 0.16/0.32/0.48, plus dust puffs.

effects.name: Falling leaves
effects.how: 2–3 px leaf frames (4 rotations) drift from visible tree canopies and 9 wind-blown leaves wrap across the view (16–27 units/s right, 7 units/s down).

effects.name: Level-up ring
effects.how: A 1-px pixel ring #ffd25a squashed to half height grows from radius 6 to 40 around the hero, plus 14 radial sparkles and 6 leaves.

ui.summary: Nailed wooden planks: #8f5c34 panels with horizontal grain lines, 3 px dark border #2b170f, bevel (inset light #b97f4b / dark #5e3820), four 3×3 cream nail heads in the corners and a hard 4 px drop shadow. Bars are inset dark troughs with banded flat fills (no gradients). Text is pixel fonts with chunky 8-direction text-shadow outlines. Level-up cards are parchment (#f6e6bc → #ead096) with a red pin.

motion: Hero walk: 4 frames, advance 1 frame per 10 world units moved (≈ 9 fps at 92 units/s); idle: 2 frames at 2.2 fps (head bob 1 px, scarf flap).

Small enemy walk: 4 frames at anim × 1.6 (≈ 6 fps); fast ghost: 4 frames at 6 fps, hovers 3 ± 1.5 units on a 3 rad/s sine, drawn at 86 % opacity; brute: 4 frames at ≈ 2.6 fps with a dust puff on each foot-fall.
Bob and offsets are whole pixels only (Math.round); everything snaps to the art-pixel grid, including the camera.
Hurt: white silhouette while hurtT > 0.55, then 18 Hz blink at 35 % alpha during invulnerability.
Carved face glow flickers: a noise(t × 9) > 0.62 switches to the brighter glow ramp for a frame or two.
Damage numbers: 3×5 (crit 5×6) bitmap digits with 1-px outline + drop row, pop up 2–3 px for 0.08 s then fade.
do: Render everything into a low-res buffer at 1 art pixel per world unit and upscale by an integer factor with imageSmoothingEnabled = false.
Build sprites procedurally into a pixel grid: ellipse/leaf primitives lit by the one shared light, quantised into hue-shifted ramps.
Let the baker add a 1-px outline coloured from the neighbouring pixels, darkened toward #24162a.
Give the ground height: grass edges get a bright rim or dark lip, paths and soil a 2-px dithered shadow band under the grass.
Scatter leaf-litter carpets in the tree's own colour under every tree; use fbm noise so meadows show three greens.
Use stepped (3-ring) additive glow discs instead of radial gradients.
Finish with the warm soft-light grade and the plum multiply vignette.
Keep pixel decals tiny (1–7 px) and give them 1-px multiply shadow pixels.
dont: Don't use smooth gradients, blur, or canvas strokes/arcs on sprites — it breaks the pixel grid.
Don't draw at fractional coordinates or upscale by non-integer factors.
Don't use black outlines or pure black shadows; shadows are plum (40,22,56) at 36 %/24 % alpha.
Don't light sprites from different directions; every ramp assumes top-left light.
Don't cover the ground with flat colour; without tufts, rims and specks it looks like a placeholder.
Don't add neon or cold saturated colours outside the ghost/ice family.
Don't mix pixel scales (e.g. 2× sprites over 1× ground).
performance: All sprites (hero 2 glow variants × 4 walk + 2 idle × 2 facings, enemies, flash silhouettes, trees, props, icons, digits) are baked once in init into small canvases; per frame only drawImage blits happen at integer positions into the low-res buffer, then one nearest-neighbour upscale. The ground is the hot spot: each 256×256 chunk evaluates several fbm fields on a 4-unit grid (bilinear), a per-pixel material map with SDF fields and stamps, so it is built as a generator that yields every 32 rows and is cached. The screen overlays (grade + vignette) are pre-rendered once per buffer size.
